newsitem.title: CHINA: WEEK AHEAD - HK stocks expected to consolidate.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - HK stocks expected to consolidate.

text.p: The Hong Kong stock market is expected to cool down and consolidate in the week ahead after enjoying record-breaking turnover and price rises last week, analysts said.

"Investors are likely to make use of the U.S. economic data released last Friday as an excuse to take profits since the market is rather overbought in the short term," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
The blue-chip Hang Seng Index surged 721.10 points, or 4.61 percent, last week to close at 16,379.22 on Friday.
The Hang Seng set an all-time high of 16,449.53 during Friday's trading and turnover hit a record HK$28.03 billion (US$3.62 billion) last Thursday.
But weaker closes of U.S. bonds and stocks last Friday on renewed inflation concerns should affect sentiment, said Ricky Tam, senior analyst at Delta Asia Securities.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average eased 28.57 points to finish at 8,194.04 after news that the U.S. economy added a hefty 316,000 new jobs in July, well above expectations for a gain of 193,000 new jobs.
The United States also reported manufacturing activity and prices paid by manufacturers both registered unexpectedly sharp rises in July.
"The latest U.S. data are strong but I don't think the U.S. will lift interest rates in August," Tam said.
Investors were tempted to take profits with a number of major corporations set to announce their earning figures this week, he added.

HSBC Holdings Plc and its subsidiary Hang Seng Bank Ltd will announce interim results on Monday while Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd and its parent Swire Pacific Ltd's half-year profit announcements were due on Wednesday and Thursday respectively.

"I bet the Hang Seng (index) would test the low of 16,000 with firm support seen at 15,800. But because of the current strong upward momentum of Hong Kong stocks, the blue-chip index could rebound by the end of the week," Tam said.
Charles Cheung, executive director at J&A Securities, also said he expected the Hang Seng to consolidate first, then swing up again to test the 16,500 level on Thursday or Friday.
"The strength on properties, which led the recent market rally, should continue with buying interest seen on the laggards of the sector and property investors," he said.

Cheung said shares of Sino Land Co Ltd, which recently announced it planned to launch sales of flats for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1998, were expected to attract buyers. Sino Land expected revenues of more than HK$16 billion (US$2.07 billion) to be generated from the sales.
The Hong Kong market should continue to enjoy money inflow from Southeast Asia and other places and the Hang Seng Index could move towards the 17,000 mark later this month, Tam said.
Mainland Chinese companies listed in Hong Kong, or H-share firms, should see some selling pressure with their reporting season to start in late August, he added.

The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index for H-shares rose 108.11 points, or 9.32 percent, to close the week at 1,268.16 on slim hopes that reforms in China's debt-burdened state enterprises would benefit their Hong Kong listing arms through restructurings.
Quality red chips were expected to continue their rebound after a brief consolidation in July, Cheung said.
Red chips are Hong Kong-incorporated firms with China's financial backing.
